page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The system provides 32 physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 128 GB of system memory at a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache per core. Local storage is not included, requiring cloud block storage for data persistence. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core processing performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving results in the top 25% of tested servers. Extended instruction workloads such as cryptographic operations, ray tracing, and image processing also perform strongly. However, uncached memory bandwidth read and write speeds perform in the middle 50%, reflecting potential memory throughput bottlenecks under heavy uncached access patterns. Small LLM prompt processing with a 135M model yields strong execution rates, whereas medium LLM workloads with a 7B model operate at average performance levels.

Due to its high virtual core density paired with a lean memory footprint, the instance offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy parallel workloads that do not require massive per-core RAM allocations or attached local NVMe drives. Highly multithreaded processing tasks, software compilation, database transaction processing, and CPU-based media rendering are well aligned with its technical profile.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processors featuring 32 physical cores, 64 vCPUs running at 2.55 GHz, and 128 GB of memory. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, this instance lacks local disk storage, relying on attached cloud storage solutions. Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU capacity, PassMark scores, and cryptographic performance within the top 25% tier, though uncached memory bandwidth and single-core tasks remain in the average tier. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU configuration delivers solid compute density, making it cost-efficient for parallel CPU processing, software compilation, database operations, and small-model inference tasks where massive memory overhead is unnecessary.
